cases.prompt: update everything on my mac
upgrade my brew packages and clean up
run my regular maintenance pass on this machine
keep my dev tools current - do the weekly update
brew outdated shows a bunch, bring things up to date safely
update app store apps and macos from the terminal
reclaim disk space from old brew versions and caches
why didn't brew upgrade update chrome and vscode?
update oh-my-zsh, my node versions and global tools too
install homebrew on this new mac
set up a Brewfile for the first time
upgrade this project's npm dependencies
update my macos to the new major version and migrate everything
brew doctor says my install is broken, fix homebrew
set up my whole mac for development
docker system prune everything now
bump the version in package.json and cut a release
Run a full but safe update pass on my dev machine.
expected_behavior: asks about timing first (not right before a release/demo) or at least warns, then runs brew update, brew outdated (showing the list before upgrading), brew upgrade
explains cask auto_updates semantics: self-updating apps are skipped by design; --greedy only on request
runs cleanup (brew cleanup, brew autoremove) and mas update; macOS softwareupdate only with explicit consent and a restart warning
updates the shell/runtime layer that exists: omz update, runtime managers (nvm/mise), uv tools, pipx, rustup, gh extensions - detecting what's installed rather than assuming
skips pinned/major-version-sensitive things (postgresql@N majors) and reports exactly what changed and what was deferred

cases.prompt: chrome and vs code never update through brew upgrade - broken?
expected_behavior: explains auto_updates casks self-update and plain brew upgrade skips them intentionally
shows brew upgrade --cask --greedy (or --greedy-auto-updates) as the opt-in, with the downside (re-downloads apps that already updated themselves)
recommends letting self-updaters do their job as the default

cases.prompt: my disk is filling up, claw back space from dev tooling
expected_behavior: starts read-only: docker system df, du on caches, brew cleanup --dry-run before deleting anything
safe reclaims: brew cleanup (and -s), brew autoremove, npm cache verify, xcrun simctl delete unavailable if Xcode present
treats docker system prune as destructive: shows what would go, warns volumes are excluded by default and --volumes deletes data, requires explicit confirmation

cases.prompt: set this machine up so updates are a one-command habit
expected_behavior: offers topgrade via brew with a reviewed ~/.config/topgrade.toml that disables risky steps (system/mas at minimum) rather than default-everything
alternative: a small documented routine (brew update/upgrade/cleanup + bundle check) if the user prefers no extra tool
keeps the Brewfile in sync (brew bundle dump with confirm-before-force) after upgrades
